title: COP31: Climate deal in doubt as EU, others reject draft declaration
summary: The climate summit is in its second day of overtime, despite weeks of negotiations. Nations are divided over a draft text that doesn't mention fossil fuels, the main cause of global warming. DW has…
byline: Jenipher Camino Gonzalez, Emmy Sasipornkarn, Nik Martin, Dmytro Hubenko, Patrick Große, Mark Hallam, Karl Sexton

image.caption: Despite weeks of talks and an extension, a deal has remain elusiveImage: Khalil Hamra/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Panama rejects draft decision, saying it 'should be based on science'
Panama's representative said the Central American nation was amongst those who suffer most from the consequences and issue of climate justice.
Panamanian Environment Minister Juan Carlos Navarro said the talks were being held hostage by a "petroleum mafia" and need to be reformed.
He said science must be the basis for the cover decision, adding that those who contributed to this crisis must shoulder the responsibility to deal with it.
"We are running out of time," Navarro told attendees. "Panama cannot support this decision. The planet cannot continue to wait."
